description: Nuages, givrage, turbulence, orages, vent et état de piste, pour décrire le temps sans les codes METAR.

fiches.question: Cloud covering the whole sky.
fiches.explication: Overcast at 800 feet, light rain.

fiches.question: The height of the base of the lowest layer of cloud covering more than half the sky.
fiches.explication: The ceiling is below minima, we will hold.

fiches.question: Very fine rain made of small, closely spaced drops.
fiches.explication: Light drizzle and mist at the airport.

fiches.question: Rain or snow that starts and stops suddenly, falling from convective clouds.
fiches.explication: Expect snow showers on the approach.

fiches.question: Balls or lumps of ice falling from a thunderstorm cloud.
fiches.explication: We flew through hail, request an inspection after landing.

fiches.question: Rain and snow falling together, or, in American usage, small ice pellets.
fiches.explication: Sleet is forecast for the evening.

fiches.question: Rain that freezes on contact with a cold surface.
fiches.explication: Freezing rain is the worst case for icing.

fiches.question: Rain or snow that falls from a cloud but evaporates before reaching the ground.
fiches.explication: Virga under the cloud base may mean strong downdrafts.

fiches.question: A towering cloud that produces thunderstorms.
fiches.explication: A line of cumulonimbus is building to the west.

fiches.question: A cumulus growing quickly upwards, which may become a thunderstorm.
fiches.explication: Towering cumulus near the final approach.

fiches.question: The height of the bottom of a cloud.
fiches.explication: The cloud base is lifting slowly.

fiches.question: The height of the top of a cloud layer.
fiches.explication: Can you give us the cloud tops?

fiches.question: Cloud covering three to four eighths of the sky.
fiches.explication: Scattered at 2,000 feet, broken at 4,000.

fiches.question: Cloud covering five to seven eighths of the sky.
fiches.explication: Broken cloud at 1,500 feet.

fiches.question: Water droplets in the air that reduce visibility below 1,000 metres.
fiches.explication: Fog is expected to form after midnight.

fiches.question: Water droplets in the air that reduce visibility to between 1,000 and 5,000 metres.
fiches.explication: Visibility 3,000 metres in mist.

fiches.question: Dry particles such as dust or smoke that reduce visibility.
fiches.explication: Haze makes the runway hard to see into the sun.

fiches.question: The boundary between two air masses of different temperature.
fiches.explication: A cold front will pass over the airport this afternoon.

fiches.question: (Of the weather) to get better, as clouds disappear.
fiches.explication: The fog should clear up by noon.

fiches.question: The build-up of ice on the aircraft.
fiches.explication: Moderate icing reported between flight level 80 and 120.

fiches.question: Rough, milky ice formed when small supercooled droplets freeze instantly.
fiches.explication: We picked up some rime ice on the wipers.

fiches.question: Hard, glassy ice formed when large supercooled droplets spread before freezing.
fiches.explication: Clear ice is heavy and hard to see.

fiches.question: (Of water) still liquid at a temperature below zero degrees.
fiches.explication: Supercooled droplets freeze on impact.

fiches.question: Removing ice, frost or snow from the aircraft before take-off.
fiches.explication: We need de-icing before departure.

fiches.question: Preventing ice from forming.
fiches.explication: Engine anti-icing is on.

fiches.question: The estimated time a de-icing or anti-icing fluid will keep protecting the aircraft.
fiches.explication: Our holdover time will run out if we wait much longer.

fiches.question: A thin coating of ice crystals formed on a cold surface.
fiches.explication: There is frost on the upper wing surface.

fiches.question: Turbulence at high altitude without any cloud, often near the jet stream.
fiches.explication: Reports of clear air turbulence at flight level 370.

fiches.question: Light, rapid, rhythmic bumpiness without noticeable changes in altitude.
fiches.explication: Light chop at our level.

fiches.question: Turbulence causing large, abrupt changes in altitude or attitude, with possible momentary loss of control.
fiches.explication: We encountered severe turbulence, two cabin crew are injured.

fiches.question: The turbulence left behind an aircraft by its wingtip vortices.
fiches.explication: Caution wake turbulence, you are following a heavy.

fiches.question: Airflow over a mountain range that forms waves, with strong up- and downdrafts.
fiches.explication: Mountain wave activity is causing altitude deviations.

fiches.question: A narrow band of very strong wind at high altitude.
fiches.explication: We have a 150-knot tailwind in the jet stream.

fiches.question: (Informal) Uncomfortable because of turbulence.
fiches.explication: It's a bit bumpy at flight level 350.

fiches.question: (Of a flight) without turbulence.
fiches.explication: Any reports of a smooth ride higher up?

fiches.question: A strong current of air moving downwards.
fiches.explication: We lost 500 feet in a downdraft.

fiches.question: A strong current of air moving upwards.
fiches.explication: A strong updraft pushed us above our level.

fiches.question: (Of a thunderstorm) hidden inside other layers of cloud.
fiches.explication: Embedded cumulonimbus along the route.

fiches.question: A line of thunderstorms moving together, often ahead of a cold front.
fiches.explication: A squall line is approaching the airport.

fiches.question: A small, intense downdraft that spreads out violently near the ground.
fiches.explication: A microburst alert is in force for runway 27.

fiches.question: A sudden change in wind speed or direction over a short distance.
fiches.explication: We had windshear on short final and went around.

fiches.question: A brief, sudden increase in wind speed.
fiches.explication: A strong gust lifted the wing on touchdown.

fiches.question: The aircraft being hit by lightning.
fiches.explication: We had a lightning strike, no damage reported.

fiches.question: A glow of electrical discharge seen on the windscreen or the wingtips in stormy weather.
fiches.explication: St Elmo's fire was dancing on the windscreen.

fiches.question: The radar that shows precipitation ahead of the aircraft.
fiches.explication: Our weather radar shows a large cell ahead.

fiches.question: To leave the planned route, for example to avoid weather.
fiches.explication: Request to deviate 20 miles left of track due to weather.

fiches.question: The flat, spreading top of a mature cumulonimbus.
fiches.explication: Stay clear of the anvil, hail can fall from it.

fiches.question: The leading edge of cold air spreading out from a thunderstorm.
fiches.explication: The gust front reached the airport before the rain.

fiches.question: A sudden heavy fall of rain.
fiches.explication: A downpour reduced the visibility to 800 metres.

fiches.question: (Of clouds) to grow larger and taller.
fiches.explication: Cells are building up to the west.

fiches.question: A single thunderstorm or area of storm activity.
fiches.explication: There is a cell right over the field.

fiches.question: (Of clouds or storms) to break up and disappear.
fiches.explication: The storm is expected to dissipate within the hour.

fiches.question: The nose cone that covers the weather radar antenna.
fiches.explication: Hail cracked the radome.

fiches.question: A wind blowing across the runway.
fiches.explication: The crosswind is above our limit for this runway.

fiches.question: A wind blowing from behind the aircraft.
fiches.explication: A ten-knot tailwind on landing is our limit.

fiches.question: A wind blowing towards the front of the aircraft.
fiches.explication: A strong headwind will add 30 minutes to the flight.

fiches.question: (Of the wind) to change direction clockwise.
fiches.explication: The wind is expected to veer to the north-west.

fiches.question: (Of the wind) to change direction anticlockwise (US: counterclockwise).
fiches.explication: The wind is backing to the south.

fiches.question: (Of the wind) changing direction often.
fiches.explication: Wind variable at 3 knots.

fiches.question: The distance at which a pilot on the runway centreline can see the runway markings or lights.
fiches.explication: Runway visual range 550 metres, improving.

fiches.question: A condition in which snow and cloud make the horizon and the ground impossible to see.
fiches.explication: A whiteout made the visual approach impossible.

fiches.question: Strong wind carrying dust or sand that greatly reduces visibility.
fiches.explication: A dust storm has closed the airport.

fiches.question: A runway covered with water, snow, slush or ice.
fiches.explication: With a contaminated runway our landing distance doubles.

fiches.question: Partly melted snow mixed with water.
fiches.explication: Two centimetres of slush on the runway.

fiches.question: A report of how well an aircraft can brake on the runway.
fiches.explication: Braking action reported medium to poor.

fiches.question: Water that collects on the runway surface and does not drain away.
fiches.explication: Patches of standing water on the second half of the runway.

fiches.question: Tyres losing contact with the runway on a layer of water.
fiches.explication: We may have been aquaplaning, the braking felt weak.

fiches.question: (Of the wind) increasing and decreasing suddenly.
fiches.explication: Wind 270 degrees, 15 knots, gusting 30.

fiches.question: (Of the wind) to become stronger.
fiches.explication: The wind is expected to pick up this afternoon.

fiches.question: (Of the wind) to become weaker.
fiches.explication: We'll wait for the wind to die down.

fiches.question: With no wind at all.
fiches.explication: Wind calm, QNH 1013.
